note: Errata 262. Tyler, 2026-11-10, shown four rooms graded beside themselves: "I like the direction. I think it would be a nice way to differentiate different rooms from each other, so they don't all look exactly the same." Each room here leans its shadows and mid-tones toward a colour of its own; its lamps and what they light keep their warmth. `tint` is the colour leaned to, `strength` how far (0 to 1), `saturate` a little more of whatever colour is there. tools/art/room-grade.py applies it to the room's plate, and to every picture cut from that plate, from the untouched originals in art/staging/room-grade/originals/. A room not listed is as it was painted: the Nugget, the mercantile, the livery and the Colonel's rooms are the warm and the red the others are told apart from.

hotel_lobby.why: green: its wallpaper and its settee

archive.why: cold blue: dust, and one barred window

church.why: a little cool: whitewash by moonlight; lightly, its pews keep their warmth

clarion.why: ink blue: a print shop at night

thads_room.why: teal: the green it already has, by a cold window

nugget_back.why: green: the shade of the lamp over the judges' table

schoolhouse.why: slate: chalk and an unlit stove

barbers.why: pale teal: enamel and a mirror

undertaker.why: a little more of the pale green it has
